topLine: A relatively quiet day in NSW state politics, with the Minns government rolling out a run of infrastructure and services announcements — West Dapto housing infrastructure, the Rouse Hill Hospital build and new Bella Vista schools — and a threatened week-long passenger rail strike suspended at the last minute after a Fair Work hearing. Pre-election positioning continues at the edges, with a Central Coast candidate naming row and a potential independent-style run flagged in Newcastle. Much of the national political attention sits on Saturday's Victorian election.

Much of the national political attention sits on Saturday's Victorian election.
briefing.localWatch: The Property Council is pushing for the Illawarra Shoalhaven to be designated a major growth corridor with aligned housing, transport and jobs planning, and better roads and transport around Nowra and Bomaderry. In Kiama, a controversially rezoned 14.26-acre site at Caliope Street has been listed for sale, while Shoalhaven City Council has set up a new group to guide its disability inclusion work.

stories.headline: Roads, rail, and a bold new vision: how Nowra could become a major growth hub
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports the Property Council is calling on the NSW government to designate the Illawarra Shoalhaven a major growth corridor, with planning for housing, transport and jobs brought into alignment. The report frames the push around improved roads and transport for Nowra and Bomaderry.

stories.headline: Controversially rezoned Kiama site hits the market amid community backlash
stories.summary: A 14.26-acre site at 2 Caliope Street, Kiama has been listed for sale following rezoning approval, the Illawarra Mercury reports. The paper describes community backlash over the rezoning and developer interest in the parcel.

stories.headline: New group will guide Council’s actions on disability inclusion
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council announces a new group to guide the council's work on disability inclusion.

stories.headline: Election chicanery accusations over new candidate’s name
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports that Labor has been accused of a "cynical trick" in naming Lisa Wicks as its candidate for the Central Coast seat of Terrigal. No further detail of the claims is available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: 'We'll find that out': Newcastle publican teases state election run
stories.summary: Newcastle publican Luke Tilse has told the Newcastle Herald there is a small chance he will contest the 2027 NSW state election. He says he intends to press Newcastle issues he believes require action from the state government.

stories.headline: NSW train strike suspended at eleveth hour
stories.summary: The ABC reports that planned industrial action by NSW passenger rail workers was suspended after a Fair Work hearing. Workers had been due to walk off the job from midnight Friday as part of week-long action in an enterprise bargaining dispute.

stories.headline: Infrastructure investment to support future housing growth in West Dapto
stories.summary: The NSW government says it is allocating $1.4 million to Wollongong City Council for the Northcliffe Drive Extension, which it links to accelerating nearly 850 new homes and supporting a further 19,500 homes across the broader West Dapto area. The Illawarra Mercury reports the council will borrow $28 million to buy land for the extension, with the state contribution going towards interest on that loan, and describes the project as enabling the closure of a level crossing the paper calls "dangerous".

stories.headline: Plan for 200ha kelp farm off NSW coast sparks debate
stories.summary: The NSW Independent Planning Commission is considering a proposal for the state's first commercial kelp farm, south of Eden, the ABC reports. The broadcaster says the proposal has drawn public submissions on both sides.

stories.headline: Australia's largest proposed vegetation-fuelled power plant rejected again
stories.summary: A court has dismissed an appeal by the proponent of what would have been Australia's largest modern biomass generator, in the NSW Hunter Valley, according to the ABC.

stories.headline: Minns Government making significant construction progress on long-awaited Rouse Hill Hospital
stories.summary: The NSW government reports construction progress on the $910 million Rouse Hill Hospital in Sydney's north-west. The ministerial release contrasts the project with what it describes as unfulfilled hospital commitments by the former Coalition government.

stories.headline: First look at brand new public primary school, high school and long day care in Bella Vista
stories.summary: The NSW government has released designs for a new public high school and primary school at Bella Vista. The release says the site would also host one of the first 100 public long day care centres promised under a re-elected Minns Labor government.

stories.headline: The election stunt that backfired on the Greens
stories.summary: In an opinion piece for The Daily Telegraph, James O'Doherty argues that an election stunt backfired on the Greens, writing that even within the party a candidate is seen to "protest too much". Only the headline is available, and the argument is the columnist's view.

elsewhere.text: Ben Raue's Tally Room reports final MRP projections for Saturday's Victorian election showing the Coalition on 55 seats, Labor 13, One Nation 12 and the Greens 8 — a useful reminder of how far seat projections can move late in a campaign.
Victoria's Coalition released its costings and key policy announcements two days from polling day, the ABC reports, after about 1.6 million Victorians had already voted.
